sections.skill: Explain tenant duties and rights and evaluate renters insurance

questions.prompt: Jen's belongings are stolen from her apartment. The landlord has building insurance. Which policy covers HER belongings?

choices.text: Her car insurance, for anything inside a home

questions.intro: A landlord's insurance covers the building, not tenants' belongings. Renters insurance covers your personal property (for theft, fire, and other listed causes) and liability if someone is injured in your home or you damage others' property. It often costs about $10–$25 a month.
questions.feedback: Tenant belongings are covered only by the tenant's renters insurance.
questions.topic: Tenant responsibilities, rights, and renters insurance

misconceptions.B: Covers the building, not tenant property

questions.prompt: Jen's renters policy costs $16 a month with a $500 deductible. A fire destroys $4,000 of her belongings (covered). How much does the insurer pay?
questions.intro: A premium is what you pay for the policy. A deductible is the amount you pay toward a claim before insurance pays the rest.

questions.prompt: Which is usually the TENANT's responsibility?

choices.text: Fixing a broken furnace or a leaking water heater herself
Keeping the unit clean and reporting problems promptly

questions.correct_answer: Keeping the unit clean and reporting problems promptly
questions.intro: Tenants generally must pay rent on time, keep the unit clean, avoid damage, follow the lease, and report repairs. Landlords generally must keep the unit safe and livable (heat, water, structural repairs) and follow notice rules.
questions.feedback: Tenants keep the unit clean and report problems.

questions.prompt: In winter, Jen's heat stops working. What should she do FIRST?

choices.text: Notify the landlord in writing and keep a copy
Hire a contractor and deduct any cost she chooses

questions.correct_answer: Notify the landlord in writing and keep a copy
questions.intro: Landlords must keep homes habitable, including heat. Tenants should report problems in writing and keep records. State law sets remedies if repairs are not made.
questions.feedback: A written notice creates a record and starts the repair process.
questions.topic: Tenant responsibilities, rights, and renters insurance

misconceptions.A: Can violate the lease without proper steps

sections.relationship: Renters insurance questions depend on distinguishing a premium from a deductible.

questions.prompt: What is an insurance PREMIUM?

choices.text: The amount paid regularly to keep the policy
The amount the policyholder pays toward each claim first

questions.correct_answer: The amount paid regularly to keep the policy
questions.intro: The premium is the price of insurance, paid monthly or yearly. The deductible is what you pay out of pocket on a claim before insurance pays.
questions.feedback: The premium is the regular cost of the policy.
questions.topic: Tenant responsibilities, rights, and renters insurance

questions.prompt: What is a DEDUCTIBLE?

choices.text: The monthly cost of the policy
The most the insurer will pay
The amount you pay on a claim before insurance pays
A bonus the insurer pays you when you file no claims

questions.correct_answer: The amount you pay on a claim before insurance pays
questions.feedback: The deductible comes out of your pocket on each claim.

questions.prompt: "Replacement cost" coverage pays to replace items with new ones. "Actual cash value" pays…

choices.text: double the original price, to cover the cost of shopping
what the items were worth after depreciation
the price of a used item of any age

questions.correct_answer: what the items were worth after depreciation
questions.intro: Policies may pay replacement cost (new item) or actual cash value (replacement cost minus depreciation). Replacement cost policies usually cost more.

questions.prompt: A 4-year-old TV would cost $1,000 to replace with a similar new one today. The policy figures its depreciation at 60%. Under actual cash value, before the deductible, what is it worth?
questions.intro: Actual cash value = today's replacement cost − depreciation. Replacement cost coverage pays the full replacement cost instead.

sections.skill: Tenant rights and when to get help

questions.prompt: Can a landlord in most states change the locks to force a tenant out without a court order?

choices.text: Yes, any time the rent is even one day past due
No; self-help evictions are generally illegal
Yes, if the lease allows it

questions.correct_answer: No; self-help evictions are generally illegal
questions.intro: In most states, including New Jersey, landlords must go through the court eviction process; lockouts and utility shutoffs to force tenants out are generally illegal.
questions.feedback: Evictions require court process; lockouts are generally illegal.
questions.topic: Tenant responsibilities, rights, and renters insurance

misconceptions.C: Believes notice replaces a court order

questions.intro: Leases and state or local laws usually require reasonable notice before non-emergency entry.
